Class TradeEventPublisher

java.lang.Object
app.order.event.TradeEventPublisher
@Component @ConditionalOnProperty(name="app.events.enabled", havingValue="true", matchIfMissing=true) public class TradeEventPublisher extends Object
Publishes each OrderResolvedEvent to the "trade-events" topic after the transaction that resolved the order has committed.

The message key is the account id, so Kafka places all of one account's events on the same partition in submission order. The body is the event serialised as JSON.

Publishing can never change the outcome of an order. Spring rethrows an exception from an after-commit listener to the caller even though the transaction is already committed, so this method catches everything the send can throw synchronously and logs it; an asynchronous failure arrives in the completion callback and is logged there. A broker that is down delays the response by at most the producer's max.block.ms. The order, its fill and its audit trail are already durable by then (BR-09).

Absent when app.events.enabled is false, which the test profile sets so that contexts without a broker never try to reach one.
